factual_methodology.summary: Bank of England, BIS, FSB and Basel sources establish current financial-sector AI use, Project Logos, AI-market concentration, supervisory concerns and agentic-payment questions.

novelty.summary: Moves the paradigms line beyond programmable infrastructure to delegated machine agency, focusing on principal-agent boundaries, common-model correlation and system-level observability.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: Public prose states facts and mechanisms directly, separates observed evidence from inference, includes explicit limitations and contains no internal publication-process narration.

contextual_depth.summary: Distinguishes current operating-scale AI support from controlled experiments in LLM portfolio management and from still-limited fully autonomous core trading.

visual_evidence_readiness.summary: Required visual budget and EN/PT-BR visual parity were checked; quantitative visuals use compatible units and structural visuals encode mechanisms defended in prose.

contrary_evidence: Fully autonomous trading is not described as a current dominant market structure.
The S&P 500 AI-company share is an approximate Bank of England classification, not a universal taxonomy.
limitations: Fully autonomous trading is not described as a current dominant market structure.
The S&P 500 AI-company share is an approximate Bank of England classification, not a universal taxonomy.
Project Logos is a simulation project and cannot establish live-market systemic effects before results exist.
notes: Approved in the 7 October deep editorial refresh after source, bilingual, taxonomy and visual checks.

en.title: From algorithmic markets to agentic markets: when software begins to act as an economic participant
en.deck: Autonomous AI is shifting financial automation from prediction and execution toward delegated economic action, raising new questions about agency, correlated behavior, authorization and system-wide governance.
en.regime: Financial automation is moving from human-supervised prediction and execution toward bounded delegated action by AI agents, while live core trading remains limited and supervisors focus increasingly on collective behavior.
en.key_risk: Common models, infrastructure and objectives could create correlated machine-speed behavior before institutions can reliably observe or interrupt it.

pt-BR.title: De mercados algorítmicos a mercados agênticos: quando software começa a agir como participante econômico
pt-BR.deck: IA autônoma desloca a automação financeira de previsão e execução para ação econômica delegada, criando novas questões de agência, correlação, autorização e governança sistêmica.
pt-BR.regime: Automação financeira passa de previsão e execução supervisionadas por humanos para ação delegada limitada por agentes de IA, enquanto negociação central autônoma continua restrita e supervisores focam comportamento coletivo.
pt-BR.key_risk: Modelos, infraestrutura e objetivos comuns podem criar comportamento correlacionado em velocidade de máquina antes que instituições consigam observá-lo ou interrompê-lo.
